pr.title: Review a pull request's head with an agent and no session, through project review run
pr.head: 5c2875417c172701e216d880e72ee6bb105379b0

summary: Projector normally needs a running agent session to review a pull request. This layer adds project review run, which starts an agent for one ready head, checks that it published a verdict, and reports failure when it did not.

The runner supports Claude Code, Codex, or a configured command. It also lets existing review readers recognize a configured bot account and lets the review job leave a checked summary for a separate job that can push it. The action and this repository’s workflow arrive in the layers above.

All three earlier findings are now verified fixed. The runner recognizes verdicts on newer pushed heads, handles Windows timeouts, and protects cleanup ownership through worktree removal. The configured gate and 49 focused tests passed; this head is signed off with no remaining findings or suggestions.

cards.title: The pieces of a CI review
cards.html:
• Reviewer: the GitHub account that posts the review.
  • Loop: the session or runner ID that owns local review state and published-review records.
  • Handoff: a summary and diff written to a folder for another job to publish.

cards.title: Validation on this head
cards.html:
• The configured gate passed: plugin validation, 256 hook tests, type-checking, diff checks, and exact-head GitHub check.
  • All 49 focused runner, finish, and handover tests passed.
  • A real temporary Git check refuses setup while removal holds the lock, then preserves the following review’s worktree, state, and lock after release.
  • The new cleanup-ordering regression fails against the preceding finish implementation.

cards.title: All findings verified fixed
cards.html:
• A newly published verdict on a newer head counts; earlier review IDs do not.
  • Timeout termination uses the appropriate process-group behavior, with a mocked Windows check.
  • Cleanup checks the current owner under the mutex and removes its worktrees before releasing the lock; a new review keeps its own resources.
  • No additional finding or suggestion remains. Checks used local fixtures and mocked GitHub responses.

groups.title: Count the account that posts the review
intro: A workflow token can act as a bot without belonging to a GitHub user, so the ordinary user lookup can fail. The identity helper now accepts PROJECTOR_TOKEN_LOGIN after GitHub returns that specific integration-token refusal; a person’s successful lookup still wins.

review.reviewers names additional GitHub accounts whose labeled Projector verdicts count. The CLI, watcher, and site apply the same list so a trusted bot verdict can sign off a public-repository head.

files.note: Registers the reviewer-account list and runner command as typed configuration settings.
Adds bot identity and configured verdict accounts, plus guarded cleanup that removes worktrees before releasing ownership.

checks.text: RunnerTokenTests passed: the environment fallback does not rename a successful person-token lookup, and an active token is reused only for its matching account.
The real-Git check blocks overlapping same-head setup during removal. A following setup succeeds after release and retains its worktree, lock and state.

files.note: Reads configured reviewer accounts from live checkouts and uses them for sign-off and suggestion events.
Lets the review pages count verdicts from configured accounts alongside repository members.
Checks token fallback, matching-account token reuse, and configured bot verdicts.
Checks that the configured bot suppresses unreviewed work while an unlisted account does not.
Checks that the site recognizes a configured bot without trusting an unlisted reviewer.

groups.title: Run one review without a conversation
intro: project review run reads the pull request, refuses forks and drafts, skips an already reviewed head unless re-review is requested, and starts a preset or configured command. The environment gives the agent the model, loop, scratch folder, and any start comment to replace.

The runner accepts a new verdict on a head pushed while the agent runs, excludes earlier review IDs, and shares portable process helpers with the core. Failed-run cleanup checks the current owner under the review mutex and removes its worktrees before releasing ownership, so a following review cannot lose its worktree.

files.note: Shares process-group creation and termination between the runner and bounded subprocess callers.

checks.text: The mocked Windows regression verifies taskkill for the process tree and a final wait for the agent. The POSIX path still kills the process group and now tolerates a group that already exited.

files.note: Starts the agent and delegates failed-run cleanup with an explicit owner loop.

checks.text: The newer-head and Windows regressions pass. Failed-run cleanup uses the current-owner fence and retains the lock until worktree removal is complete.

files.note: Exposes the runner options and passes reviewer configuration through review, site, and summary commands.
Covers runner refusal, verdict detection, cleanup ownership, timeout and overlapping-worktree behavior.

checks.text: All 49 focused runner, finish and handover tests pass. The new ordering regression fails when the prior finish implementation is restored in memory.

groups.title: Let another job publish the summary
intro: A review job does not need permission to push repository contents. When PROJECTOR_SUMMARY_HANDOFF names a folder and the site is hosted, summary publication validates the page and writes its JSON and diff there instead of pushing.

The later publishing job can require a particular pull request number with --pr. Publication also checks the current head before replacing GitHub summary links, while older-head summaries remain available on the site.

files.note: Shares pre-publication validation with handoff, reads the current head, and includes review authors in site status data.
Checks handoff files without pushes, invalid-summary refusal, wrong-PR refusal, and old-head link preservation.

checks.text: The focused summary tests passed, including a temporary bare remote whose summaries ref remains unchanged during handoff.

groups.title: Document the unattended review contract
groups.kicker: Permissions, skill behavior and plan state
intro: The headless skill takes its loop and model from the runner, skips subscriptions, and writes questions to a report because nobody can answer interactively. Its normal review and summary method still applies.

The permission configuration asks before a person’s session starts another review agent. The CLI reference describes the new runner and summary flow, while the project plan moves to in-progress and records implementation decisions.
